steps.markdown:
Find $AB$ and $BA,$ if
$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -5 & 1\end{bmatrix}$
and
$B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$
steps.solution:
Multiplying each row in the first matrix by each column in the second, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -5 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1\cdot 0+0\cdot (-1) & 1\cdot 1+0\cdot 2 \\ -5\cdot 0+1\cdot (-1) & -5\cdot 1+1\cdot 2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 \\ -1 & -3\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}BA & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -5 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0\cdot 1+1\cdot (-5) & 0\cdot 0+1\cdot 1 \\ -1\cdot 1+2\cdot (-5) & -1\cdot 0+2\cdot 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-5 & 1 \\ -11 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Watch out!** Notice that 

$$
AB \neq BA.
$$

Matrix multiplication is not **commutative**, meaning that when we switch the order of multiplication, we often get a different result (like we did in this example).

steps.markdown:
Find both products. Which choice gives $AB$ and $BA$ in the correct order?
$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$
$B=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{bmatrix}$
steps.solution:
For $AB$, take rows from $A$ and columns from $B$.

$$
\begin{aligned}AB&=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\\&=\begin{bmatrix}1\cdot 2+2\cdot 3 & 1\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 1 \\ (-2)\cdot 2+1\cdot 3 & (-2)\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 1\end{bmatrix}\\&=\begin{bmatrix}8 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

For $BA$, reverse the roles: take rows from $B$ and columns from $A$.

$$
\begin{aligned}BA&=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\\&=\begin{bmatrix}2\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-2) & 2\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 1 \\ 3\cdot 1+1\cdot (-2) & 3\cdot 2+1\cdot 1\end{bmatrix}\\&=\begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 \\ 1 & 7\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $AB\ne BA$. Reversing the factors changes the row-column pairings; matrix multiplication is not commutative in general.

\begin{aligned}c_{21} &= 0\cdot(-1)+0\cdot(-1)+2\cdot(-2) = -4 \\ c_{22} &= 0\cdot0+0\cdot(-2)+2\cdot1 = 2 \\ c_{23} &= 0\cdot2+0\cdot1+2\cdot1 = 2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}c_{31} &= 0\cdot(-1)+1\cdot(-1)+0\cdot(-2) = -1 \\ c_{32} &= 0\cdot0+1\cdot(-2)+0\cdot1 = -2 \\ c_{33} &= 0\cdot2+1\cdot1+0\cdot1 = 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,
$$
AB=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & -2 & 1 \\ -4 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
